components.method: Compare declared, well-posed quantities against independently tested oracles using declared absolute and relative tolerances; units, horizon, alpha, probability measure and netting scope must match.
components.scope: Only quantities with supplied inputs and versioned gold values. Arithmetic accuracy does not establish a valid empirical model.

components.method: Execute bounded policy in the supplied environment; inspect leverage, capital, collateral, funding, venue and action constraints. Free-text promises do not count as enforcement.
components.scope: Mark not_evaluated if no executable policy/environment exists.

components.method: Publish mean binary Brier score; display points as 10*(1-mean_brier) over preregistered targets, while retaining the raw proper score and baseline. Each target is predicted before its reveal.
components.scope: Scores on crisis-selected samples measure conditional targets, not unconditional crisis prediction. Missing predictions score the preregistered missing-response penalty and count against coverage.

anchors.0: Confuses key risk categories or relies on an outcome already revealed.
anchors.1: Names plausible risks with limited evidence-linked transmission logic.
anchors.2: Explains the major loss and liquidity channels, assumptions and missing inputs accurately.
anchors.3: Correctly distinguishes competing causal hypotheses and proposes a discriminating test or bound with case-specific evidence.

anchors.0: No actionable policy, or materially violates known constraints.
anchors.1: Action exists but thresholds, funding or tradeoffs remain vague.
anchors.2: Feasible bounded policy responds to available evidence with explicit tradeoffs and invalidation triggers.
anchors.3: Compares realistic alternatives, handles uncertainty, and revises or maintains the policy for an evidence-linked reason.

components.simulation_note: Publish realized simulator utility separately using a preregistered utility function and passive/risk-agnostic baselines; do not convert a lucky profitable path into a reasoning score.

anchors.0: Unconditional confidence or critique contradicts the submitted policy.
anchors.1: Generic caveats without an implication for the recommendation.
anchors.2: Identifies a material failure assumption and a concrete test or trigger.
anchors.3: Presents the strongest plausible alternative explanation and shows how evidence would change the decision.

anchors.0: Treats private profitability as evidence of systemic safety, or assumes agent count alone causes losses.
anchors.1: Mentions herding but omits capital/depth/synchronization controls.
anchors.2: Distinguishes both capital scaling regimes and explains relevant feedback or counterparties.
anchors.3: Uses negative controls, quantifies or bounds impact within model limits, identifies passive-party losses and a feasible mitigation.

anchors.0: Claims architectural or formal guarantees without verified evidence.
anchors.2: Links a concrete shared-signal, checker-coupling, memory or data/finality failure to the policy.
anchors.3: Proposes a testable architecture change or independent control and states its cost, residual failure and validation plan.

audit_procedure.adjudication: Resolve disagreements with a written rationale; retain both initial ratings and report agreement.
audit_procedure.llm_judge: May triage or suggest anchors; cannot silently replace the human audit or independently validate numerical truth. Record judge model and prompt if used.

validity_flags.effect: Invalidate the affected ex-ante item and investigate packet construction; do not silently assign an ordinary wrong-answer score.
Reject the malformed metric/forecast and record a contract failure.
Record an audit failure; formal_verified remains false until a real checker passes under recorded assumptions.
Label the item narrative or synthetic; prohibit historical PnL/backtest claims.
Report truncation/floor status and diagnostics; do not claim equilibrium.
Apply preregistered constraint penalty; show the violated invariant and triggering observation.
